title: Oncall rundown — SRE weekly reliability prep
body:
Purpose / meeting goals:
- Quick sync pre-weekly ops: align on SLO posture, confirm incident handoffs, surface any new outage risks.
- Decide on alert tuning for paging noise and action owners for top 3 reliability projects.

Agenda (15–20m):
1) SLO snapshot + error budget (3m)
2) Paging trend highlights and false-positive clusters (4m)
3) Top incidents last 7 days — RCA status and blockers (6m)
4) Action items + owners (2m)

SLOs / Metrics (quick numbers to paste into meeting):
- Request success SLO: 99.95% monthly target. Last 7d: 99.86% (error budget burn ~0.09%) — still healthy but trending down after Wed spike.
- p95 latency (text-generation endpoints): target 200ms, last 7d: 248ms, p99: 890ms.
- Embeddings throughputs: 99.9% latency under 120ms, current 7d avg 115ms.
- Error budget notes: small sustained burn due to two spikes; recommend no canary rollouts until stabilized.

Paging trends (what I noticed):
- Nightly 02:00–04:30 UTC pages on model-workers (gpu) for transient OOMs. Pattern: short lived (30–90s) but triggers immediate paging.
- Increase in metadata service 5xx alerts during DB failover window Tuesday (approx 20m of elevated 5xx).
- Alert noise: routing service alert for p95>300ms fired multiple times due to single-host tilt (not cluster-wide).
- Pager fatigue risk: 18 pages/day -> ~40% are noise (based on last 10 days). Need smoothing.

Top incidents (last 7 days) — brief notes + current state:
1) GPU OOM cascade (2026-03-10 01:45 UTC) — SRE-318
   - Symptom: sudden OOMs on dedicated pool, autoscaler removed nodes and then re-added; multiple requests failed with 500.
   - Probable cause: a model rollout (quantized variant) created higher transient memory due to KV cache fragmentation plus a memory leak in runtime PR #1512.
   - Current: hotfix deployed (revert runtime PR + soft eviction) reduced pages. Ongoing: run a mem-profiling job on a staging replica.
   - Blocker: reproducer data set needed (owner: Jin).

2) Metadata service flapping during DB failover (2026-03-11 20:10 UTC) — INFRA-472
   - Symptom: 5xx spike for metadata reads, affected routing decisions and caused downstream increased latency.
   - Probable cause: failover caused connection pool exhaustion + retry storm.
   - Mitigation done: backoff patch in client, temporary increase of pool size.
   - Follow-up: implement client-side circuit breaker (owner: Miguel, due 2026-03-20).

3) False-positive latency alert from route-proxy (2026-03-09/continuous)
   - Symptom: single-host CPU spike (brief) triggered p95 alert; other hosts fine.
   - Notes: alert threshold is cluster p95 across one-minute windows — too tight.
   - Action: tune alert to 5m window and require >25% of hosts above threshold before page (owner: Aisha).

Runbook gaps I want to call out:
- GPU OOM runbook missing a quick triage script to dump running model sizes / kv-cache size. Add snippet to Runbooks page.
- Metadata failover playbook: missing the specific client-side config to enable exponential backoff + max_retries; add config sample.

Action items (concrete, with owners & dates):
- Aisha: update route-proxy p95 alert to 5m window + host-threshold gating. Target: 2026-03-14 EOD.
- Jin: produce reproducible mem-profiling workload for the quantized model and attach to SRE-318. Target: 2026-03-16.
- Miguel: implement lightweight circuit breaker for metadata client libs (initial patch + unit tests). Target: 2026-03-20.
- Sofia: create a short postmortem draft for the GPU OOM incident (include timeline + mitigation steps). Target: 2026-03-15.
- Infra team: run a canary soak with quantized model on staging with mem-monitoring enabled (coord: Jin + Infra). Target: 2026-03-18.

Notes to self (scratchpad):
- Bring up the new Datadog dashboard snippet showing per-model p95 and per-host crash counts.
- Ask product: are there scheduled heavy embed batches this week? Could explain spike. Slack #product -> @Luca.
- Consider adding a small sampling of full traces to the p99 alert to reduce debug time.

Open questions for the sync:
- Do we block canary rollouts across Dedicated until mem-profiling? (my leaning: yes for quantized variants)
- Is the current paging escalation still acceptable for oncall rota? (we might need temporary 2-person coverage nights)
- Can infra provision a low-cost staging GPU node with detailed metrics for the reproducer?

Prep + artifacts to bring to meeting:
- Datadog: request-latency-prod (7d) snapshot, host-crash-counts, gpu-mem-usage per host.
- Jenkins: latest perf-run for quantized model (run id: 2026-03-11-qr).
- PR link: runtime PR #1512 (reverted) and notes from revert commit.
- Runbooks page link (in linked_artifacts).

Quick agenda script I will use during the sync:
- 00:00–00:30: TL;DR SLOs and key numbers.
- 00:30–03:30: Paging noise + incidents — who owns what.
- 03:30–05:30: Agree on immediate alert tuning changes.
- 05:30–06:30: Assign follow-ups and confirm due dates.

Misc scratch:
- If Jin can't reproduce mem leak by 03-16, escalate to runtime team for assisted debug (owner: Aisha).
- Revisit paging thresholds after one week of changes (follow-up meeting add to calendar: 2026-03-21).

Status: ready to present — just need Jin's reproducer and the Datadog snapshot.
